messages:
Nora (Acme): team, starting ~11:07 PDT our production traffic to Redwood's hosted inference /v1/generate started returning intermittent 5xxs. About 25-35% of calls failing, users seeing errors in the UI. Sample curl below and one raw response we captured.

Nora (Acme): ```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer sk-live-REDACTED\" \
  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \
  -d '{\"model\":\"gpt-xyz\",\"input\":\"status?\"}' -v
```

Nora (Acme): Example response: 
```
HTTP/1.1 504 Gateway Timeout
content-type: application/json
{\"error\":\"control-plane timeout\",\"trace_id\":\"rid-9c3f2a\"}
```

alice (Support): thanks @Nora, I'm escalating now. Which Redwood region are you hitting? Any more trace_ids? Also is this affecting all models or just a subset?

Nora (Acme): us-west-2. I grabbed three traces: rid-9c3f2a, rid-9c3f5d, rid-9c3f77. All models we call are affected (gpt-xyz + embeddings).

ben (SRE): looking at control-plane metrics in us-west-2: spike in latency for routing-policy and session-store RPCs, plus DB connection queue growing. From control-plane logs: 

ben (SRE): ```
[11:07:13] routing-policy GET /policy svc=router status=504 dur=30020ms trace=rid-9c3f2a
[11:07:14] session-store GET /session id=sess-11 err=\"timeout after 30s\" trace=rid-9c3f2a
[11:07:14] config-db SELECT ... err=\"pool exhausted\" used=120/120 waiters=17
```

carla (eng-oncall): I'm on pager. Config DB primary (pg-prod-usw2) shows CPU spike and maxed client connections. Looks like the control-plane began hammering the DB after a small routing-policy cache eviction storm. Will run immediate mitigations: 1) enable short-lived in-memory routing cache on control-plane nodes, 2) temporarily increase DB listen/connections and pgbouncer pool size, 3) scale session-store replicas. Starting step 1 now.

deploy-bot: deploy started by carla: enable-local-routing-cache us-west-2 rollout=4/4

carla (eng-oncall): cache enabled (TTL 45s). Observability: routing-policy read rate down ~65%. DB queue length falling.

ben (SRE): error rate on API fell from ~30% -> ~8% within 90s after cache. Still seeing occasional session-store timeouts when bursts hit. Patching client pool to increase max_conns to 250 and adding jitter to avoid synchronized reconnects. Rolling patch to control-plane clients.

deploy-bot: rolling deploy: ctrlplane-client-pool-bump -> 3/4 updated

ben (SRE): pool bump completed. pgbouncer pool increased, backlog cleared. Initiating controlled failover of config-db primary to a healthier standby to eliminate any lingering process-level issues. Running failover script now.

deploy-bot: pg_failover initiated for pg-prod-usw2

carla (eng-oncall): failover finished, new primary stable. Replica lag within 200ms. CPU and active connections normalized.

ben (SRE): sanity checks: routing-policy latencies back to normal, session-store p95 down, API 5xxs <1% now. Will monitor for 1 hour. Collected traces: [rid-9c3f2a, rid-9c3f5d, rid-9c3f77]. Dashboards snapshot: https://grafana.internal/redwood/dashboard/db/ctrlplane-usw2?orgId=1

alice (Support): Nora, can you confirm whether your traffic is normal now? Any remaining 5xxs or increased client-side retries?

Nora (Acme): running a sweep of our endpoints — looks healthy; 200s for the last 10 minutes. We did see some user-facing retries though. We'll log any anomalies and let you know.

dmitri (product): flagging potential SLA impact. @alice and @eva, please collate affected request ranges and see about offering credits if customer impact exceeds thresholds.

eva (Billing): noted — when you have the traces/IDs and time windows, we can evaluate. We'll need exact ranges (start-end timestamps) and approximate request counts.

zane (support-lead): good triage here. Capture the mitigation timeline and the config changes we applied: local routing cache enabled (TTL=45s), control-plane client pool max_conns raised to 250, pgbouncer pool increased, config-db failover. We'll include these in the postmortem.

carla (eng-oncall): immediate action items:
- eng-runtime (carla): implement sticky per-node routing cache and add circuit-breaker with short backoff for routing-policy calls.
- eng-infra (ben): design change: move to connection proxy + dynamic pooling (RFC scheduled).
- eng-auth: add fallback behavior when session-store times out (graceful anonymous session / retry token).
- product/support (alice/dmitri/eva): draft customer comms and compensation plan.

ben (SRE): arch note: root cause likely cascade: cache eviction storm -> routing-policy high QPS to config-db -> DB connection exhaustion -> session-store timeouts -> API 5xxs. We'll include detailed trace waterfall in RCA.

alice (Support): internal incident INC-2026-229 opened and assigned to eng-oncall + infra + auth. Keeping this thread open until postmortem posted.

Nora (Acme): thanks for the quick turnaround. Please include any recommendations we should take on our side to reduce retries or modify client backoff.

carla (eng-oncall): recommend exponential backoff with jitter on client side, avoid aggressive retry loops for 5xx on short windows. We'll provide guidance in the support ticket. Marking incident P1 -> monitoring, will publish postmortem in 48h.

ben (SRE): monitoring window 60m started; will close PagerDuty if stable. Traces archived to internal S3: s3://redwood-incidents/2026-02-14/ctrlplane-usw2/ (rid-9c3f2a, rid-9c3f5d, rid-9c3f77).

alice (Support): thanks everyone — leaving note to follow up on billing & postmortem. Closing customer-facing escalation but keeping internal incident open until RCA complete. :white_check_mark:
